newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates rise on flood damage reports.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates rise on flood damage reports.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates rose on Monday following reports of flood damage to the crop, brokers at the Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 variety rose to 2,700.50 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), including 10 percent sales tax, from Sunday's 2,675, broker Nasim Usman said.
"We have reports of damage to more than 100,000 375-lb bales," Usman said. Official sources say some 75,000 bales have been destroyed by floods, mainly in Punjab province.
Prices rose after spinners rushed to buy cotton after hearing reports of the damage, Usman said.

The KCA said exports had reached 1.82 million bales by August 25 since the 1995/96 season began on September 1. Dealers had registered 2.33 million bales for export with the state-run Export Promotion Bureau by June 3, the KCA said.
